workload.queryMode: one cold, entity-bound point query per tenant; no application retries
workload.seed: 100 independent graph writes each committed one setting fact; one shared graph transaction committed the same 100 tenant settings

interpretation: The tenant-per-graph layout reduced local cold pointed-read p99 by 16 ms (about 13%) in this sample while preserving 100/100 complete answers, but it still missed the 100 ms objective at 100 offered concurrent requests. It distributes aggregate demand across independent per-graph authorities; it does not scale a single hot tenant/graph. This is an application partitioning tradeoff, not transparent graph sharding or proof of infinite capacity.
limitations: One closed-loop Miniflare sample on one machine; latency is inside the local Worker RPC harness, not external network caller latency or Cloudflare placement.
No repeated trials, open-loop load, mixed writes, failure injection, multi-region test, or hosted deployment.

Different graph IDs have independent commit sequences and no cross-graph transaction-closed snapshot. Cross-tenant query aggregation would require fanout and an explicit completeness/freshness contract.
The single-graph layout used one 100-fact transaction; the per-tenant layout used 100 separate one-fact transactions. This is a read-path partition comparison, not an equivalent write-cost benchmark.
